countermeasures.name: Weekday House Pre-Cooling
countermeasures.description: Pre-cool the house from 2–4 PM before the APS weekday demand window.
countermeasures.goal: Shift HVAC cooling from the 4–7 PM APS demand window into off-peak hours.

countermeasures.name: Garage Mini-Split Peak Strategy
countermeasures.description: Set garage mini-split to 100°F from 4–7 PM instead of turning it off.
countermeasures.goal: Reduce APS peak demand while maintaining equipment protection.

countermeasures.name: Front AC Sleep Temperature
countermeasures.description: Raised Front AC sleep temperature from 71°F to 72°F.
countermeasures.goal: Reduce overnight HVAC consumption while maintaining comfort.

countermeasures.name: Front AC 75°F Peak Strategy
countermeasures.description: Changed weekday Front AC schedule to 74°F pre-cooling from 2–4 PM followed by 75°F during the APS 4–7 PM demand window.
countermeasures.goal: Reduce Front AC runtime and electrical demand during the APS demand window.

countermeasures.name: Front AC Peak Stagger Strategy
countermeasures.before: Front AC 75°F from 5–6 PM; Hall AC 75°F
countermeasures.after: Front AC 76°F from 5–6 PM; Hall AC remains 75°F
countermeasures.description: Temporarily raise the Front AC cooling target from 75°F to 76°F from 5–6 PM on the test day while leaving Hall AC at 75°F. Home Ops historical analysis identified 5–6 PM as the strongest opportunity to reduce simultaneous compressor operation.
countermeasures.goal: Reduce simultaneous Front and Hall AC compressor operation and APS demand during the 5–6 PM peak hour without materially degrading comfort or causing excessive recovery demand.
